items.followUp: What is an IP address used for in a computer network?

rubric.why: Identifies an IP address as an address assigned to a device.
rubric.description: Defines an IP address as a unique numerical address assigned to a device on a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a unique or numerical device address.

rubric.why: States the purpose of the address.
rubric.description: Explains that the address identifies or locates the device so it can communicate on a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the address to identifying or locating a device for communication.

modelAnswer: An IP address is a unique numerical address assigned to a device on a network.
It identifies the device and allows it to communicate with other devices.

items.followUp: Which HTML attribute specifies the destination of a hyperlink?

rubric.why: Identifies the HTML element used to create a hyperlink.
rubric.description: Names the anchor tag, <a>.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the <a> or anchor tag.

rubric.why: Identifies the attribute that supplies the hyperlink destination.
rubric.description: States that the href attribute specifies the link destination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming href.

modelAnswer: The anchor tag, <a>, is used to create a hyperlink in HTML.
The href attribute gives the destination of the hyperlink.

items.followUp: What information should be identified before drawing a flowchart for a problem?

rubric.why: Begins with understanding the problem to be solved.
rubric.description: Clearly understand and define the problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the problem must first be understood or defined.

rubric.why: Identifies the information the flowchart will receive.
rubric.description: Determine the required input data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the input.

rubric.why: Identifies the actions needed to solve the problem.
rubric.description: Determine the processing, operations or calculations to be performed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the required processing.

rubric.why: Identifies the expected result of the problem.
rubric.description: Determine the required output or results.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the output.

modelAnswer: First, understand and clearly define the problem to be solved.
Identify the input data required by the problem.
Determine the processing, operations or calculations that must be performed.
Identify the expected output or results; these requirements can then be arranged in logical order in the flowchart.

items.followUp: How does a router help devices communicate across different networks?

rubric.why: Identifies what a router is.
rubric.description: Defines a router as a networking device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a network device.

rubric.why: Describes its role in connecting networks.
rubric.description: States that it connects two or more networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it connects networks.

rubric.why: Describes what the router forwards.
rubric.description: States that it forwards data packets between networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the forwarding of data packets.

rubric.why: Explains how it directs data to its destination.
rubric.description: Explains that it uses destination information, such as an IP address, to select a route for the data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning IP-address-based forwarding or choosing a route.

modelAnswer: A router is a networking device that connects two or more networks.
It forwards data packets from one network to another.
It examines the destination IP address of each packet.
It selects a suitable route so that the packets reach their destination.

items.followUp: Define cyber crime and explain two examples of it.

rubric.why: Defines cyber crime as unlawful activity involving computers or the internet.
rubric.description: Defines cyber crime as an illegal activity carried out using computers, networks or the internet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a definition that identifies the activity as illegal and computer- or internet-related.

rubric.why: Identifies and explains one type of cyber crime.
rubric.description: Explains hacking as gaining unauthorized access to a computer or network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming hacking and describing unauthorized access.

rubric.why: Identifies and explains another type of cyber crime.
rubric.description: Explains phishing as using fake messages or websites to trick people into revealing information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming phishing and describing the deception used to obtain information.

rubric.why: Identifies and explains a third type of cyber crime.
rubric.description: Explains identity theft as stealing and misusing another person's personal information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming identity theft and describing the misuse of another person's information.

modelAnswer: Cyber crime is an illegal activity carried out using a computer, network or the internet.
Hacking is gaining unauthorized access to a computer or network.
Phishing uses fake messages or websites to trick people into revealing personal information.
Identity theft is stealing and misusing another person's personal information.

items.followUp: What three things are usually identified when defining a problem for a computer solution?

rubric.why: Captures the purpose of defining a problem.
rubric.description: States that defining a problem means clearly understanding and stating the problem to be solved.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying the problem is clearly understood or stated.

rubric.why: Identifies the requirements used to describe the problem.
rubric.description: Mentions identifying the required input, processing and output.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying these requirements, or equivalent wording.

modelAnswer: Defining a problem means clearly understanding and stating the problem that needs to be solved.
It includes identifying the required input, processing and expected output.

items.followUp: Why is a prototype useful when developing a software product?

rubric.why: Identifies a prototype as an early representation of the product.
rubric.description: Defines a prototype as a preliminary model or early version of a product.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as an initial model or version.

rubric.why: Explains how a prototype is used during development.
rubric.description: States that it is used to test ideas or obtain feedback before developing the final product.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning testing, requirements checking or user feedback.

modelAnswer: A prototype is a preliminary model or early version of a product.
It is used to test ideas, check requirements and obtain feedback before the final product is developed.
